title: Authentication middleware
idea: `authenticate` is middleware that turns the session cookie into `req.user`, or answers `401`. Register it once and every route after it is protected.
points: `authenticate` reads the `sid` cookie and looks the session up in Postgres.
A valid session sets `req.user`, a property later handlers read, then calls `next()`.
Routes registered before `app.use(authenticate)` stay public; routes after it need a login.
Login issues a fresh id and never adopts one the client sent.

hero.title: One check in front of every route

steps.caption: Ada's browser calls `GET /me` and attaches its `sid` cookie.
`authenticate` looks the id up in `sessions`. The row exists and has not expired, so the caller is Ada.
`authenticate` stored her on `req.user` and called `next()`. The handler answers from `req.user`.
The response travels back to the browser: `200` with Ada's id, email and role.
A later request has no cookie, or one whose session was deleted. `authenticate` finds no live session.
It sends `401` and never calls `next()`, so the handler does not run.

code.title: Login, authenticate, logout
code.caption: Real Express and Postgres. Role checks arrive later, with `requireRole`.

walk.text: Both tables, and Ada with a demo password. Cost `4` is demo-only; use a higher cost for real.
The last page's session functions: create a row, find its live user, delete a row.
`authenticate` turns the cookie into a user. No cookie, unknown id or expired session means `401`.
`/login` comes first, so it needs no cookie. Bad input is `400`; a wrong password is `401`.
Every login makes a fresh id and ignores old cookies, so a planted id never becomes valid.
`app.use(authenticate)` guards every route registered after it. Handlers read `req.user` without checking again.
The script calls its own server as a browser would: no login, bad logins, a good one, logout.

pitfalls: Register `app.use(authenticate)` after public routes like `/login`, or nobody can log in.
Stop with `return res.status(401)...`; without `return`, `next()` still runs the handler.
Mount `cookieParser()` before `authenticate`, or `req.cookies` is `undefined` and requests fail with `500`.

quiz.why: No `return` follows the `401`, so execution continues and `next()` runs too. The handler would run on a rejected request.

takeaway: Write the login check once as middleware, and handlers can trust `req.user`.

starters: Should `authenticate` query the database on every request?
